title: The Extinct “American Cheetah” Wasn’t a Cheetah After All - Nautilus
author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThe Extinct “American Cheetah” Wasn’t a Cheetah After AllAnd, unlike African cheetahs, it was a flexible carnivoreDRBy Devin Reese10:00 AM CDT on September 4, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleFrom about 2.5 million years ago to 16,000 years ago, a big cat roamed the open grasslands of North America. Its fossils show a streamlined body, long legs, and large nostrils, suggesting an animal that adapted to a life of chasing prey across the savanna like an African cheetah. Now, however, the “American cheetah” (Miracinonyx trumani) may need to be called something else. That’s because a study published today in the journal Current Biology found that it wasn’t what it appeared to be.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured Video“It’s very hard to imagine a prehistoric species we’ve never seen without comparing it to something we know,” said first author Molly Cassatt-Johnstone, a graduate student at the University of California, Santa Cruz, in a press release. Read more: “How the Fastest Land Animal in North America Got Its Need for Speed”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
